main_text.p: » qui à puppi religatus scaphā » annexā trahebat, naui quo-ad posset moderaretur: ille autē cuius merces erant, in gla-dium in naui ibidem incum-bëret[?]. Hic ille naufragus ad gubernaculum accessit, & na-ui, quoad potuit, est opitulatus. Sedatis autem fluctibus, & tempestate iam commuta-ta, nauis in portum prouehi-tur. Ille autem qui in gladiû incubuerat, leuiter saucius, fa-cile est ex uulnere recreatus. Nauim cum onere horū triū suam quisque esse dicit. Hic omnes scripto ad causam ac-cedunt, & ex nominis ui na-scitur controuersia. Nam & re-

page.notes: The "»" marks at the start of each line are printed as a running quotation mark; they are transcribed as printed. The running head at the right is heavy, partly blackletter-like type and could not be read reliably; it is marked illegible. The word "bëret" is doubtful and marked [?]. The page is printed with the long s as "f" in "fcapha" and "fcripto" and similar words; these are transcribed as "s" where the context requires it (scaphā, scripto), with the printed spelling otherwise kept.
